elements.label: But this does not mean that Moral
Philosophy has not still much to learn
from Aristotle's Ethics.
The work still remains one of the best
introductions to a study of its
important subject-matter, it spreads
before us a view of the relevant facts,
it reduces them to manageable compass
and order, it raises some of the central
problems, and makes acute and valuable
suggestions towards their solution.
Above all, it perpetually incites to
renewed and independent reflection upon
them.
But this does not mean that Moral
Philosophy has not still much to learn
from Aristotle's Ethics.
